# Treasury fixtures

Unlike the sales/supply/cost fixtures next door, these are **synthetic** —
no real bank statement PDF was available while building
`add-treasury-statement-ingestion` (finance had not yet produced one). They
exist to prove the full pipeline (PDF bytes → `pdf-parse` text extraction →
line parsing → raw rows) works end to end against a REAL PDF binary, not
just against pre-extracted line arrays the way the parser-level `.spec.ts`
files next to each parser do.

`pagbank-sample.pdf` was generated by rendering a small HTML page and
printing it to PDF with headless Chrome (`--print-to-pdf`) — a real PDF
generator, so the text layer, font embedding and page structure are all
genuine, only the transaction data itself is invented. It carries four lines
exercising: an ordinary compra with the real dash-joined wording
("Pix enviado - AMBEV"), a structurally-forced movement
("Cartão PagBank - Pagamento de Fatura"), an inflow, and a `contains`-rule
keyword line ("POSTO IPIRANGA CENTRO").

**Updated 2026-08-26 against a real PagBank statement** finance provided
(`var/exemplos-de-planilhas/.../Extratos/Extratos/Pagbank jan a junho.pdf`,
gitignored, never committed) — line shape confirmed correct (`DD/MM/YYYY`
at line start, `R$` present, the historical "-R$" concatenated-sign bug
real) with one fix: real text joins the verb and the favorecido with a
dash ("Pix enviado - X"), which this fixture now reproduces (see
`statement-line.ts`'s `stripKnownPrefix` fix, design.md D9). The other five
sources' fixtures are still being brought in line the same way — see
`add-treasury-statement-ingestion/tasks.md` §10 for progress per source.
